title: Neurocrine Biosciences Announces Key Leadership Hiring, Promotions
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Neurocrine Biosciences's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: SAN DIEGO , July 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: NBIX) today announced the appointment of three Senior Vice Presidents, further strengthening its leadership team as the company executes its next phase of growth, expands its commercial portfolio and advances one of the industry's strongest neuroscience pipelines. These appointments reflect Neurocrine's continued evolution into a diversified, multi-product biopharmaceutical company positioned to deliver sustainable long-term growth. The appointments include Bret Paulson, who joins the company as Senior Vice President, Market Access, and the promotions of David Bradfute to Senior Vice President and Global Head of Intellectual Property, and Aaron Vosburgh to Senior Vice President, Finance and Accounting. "Neurocrine is entering a new phase of growth as we expand our commercial portfolio, advance one of the industry's most productive pipelines and prepare to bring more innovative medicines to patients," said Kyle W. Gano, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer, Neurocrine Biosciences. "Successfully executing on that opportunity requires exceptional leadership across every function of our company. Bret, Aaron and David each bring outstanding expertise, judgment and a proven ability to build high-performing organizations. Together, they strengthen our ability to execute today while positioning Neurocrine for the opportunities ahead, ultimately enabling us to deliver greater value for patients, healthcare providers and shareholders." Bret Paulson is an accomplished leader with nearly 30 years of experience in the biopharmaceutical and insurance industries. He will be responsible for shaping and driving Neurocrine's global market access vision, strategy and execution to provide patient access to the company's current and future medicines, while strengthening payer partnerships and reimbursement strategies across an increasingly diversified portfolio. He joins Neurocrine after more than six years at Otsuka Pharmaceutical Companies, most recently as Vice President and Head of Market Access & Channel Strategy. Prior to that, he was Area Vice President, National Accounts at Horizon after working in the commercial organizations at Schering Plough, Eli Lilly & Company, and Amgen. Paulson earned a Bachelor of Arts in Asian studies from Brigham Young University. David Bradfute , who joined Neurocrine in 2017, has been promoted to Senior Vice President and Global Head of Intellectual Property and will also serve as Managing Director of Neurocrine Switzerland GmbH, based in the company's Basel, Switzerland, office. In his expanded role, Bradfute will lead the company's global intellectual property strategy and oversee the protection of Neurocrine's products, diversified portfolio, technology platforms, and scientific innovations. Before joining Neurocrine, Bradfute held leadership roles across the healthcare and life sciences industry, including a 13-year career at Arena Pharmaceuticals and later as Head of Legal and Intellectual Property at Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute. He earned a bachelor's degree in biochemistry from Swarthmore College, master's and doctoral degrees in biological sciences from Stanford University, and a Juris Doctor from Stanford Law School. Aaron Vosburgh , an eight-year Neurocrine employee, will oversee enterprise financial strategy, partnering with executive leadership to align capital allocation, long-range financial planning and portfolio investments with Neurocrine's strategy to advance innovation and deliver new therapies to patients. While at Neurocrine, he has helped build, scale and strengthen the company's accounting, finance, tax, treasury, and financial planning and analysis capabilities while serving as a strategic advisor on many of the company's most important financial decisions. Prior to joining Neurocrine, Vosburgh held senior finance leadership roles at Applied Proteomics, Synthetic Genomics, Verenium Corporation, and Natural Alternatives International, following the start of his career at Ernst & Young. He is a Certified Public Accountant (inactive) and earned a Bachelor of Arts in Accounting from the University of San Diego. About Neurocrine Biosciences Neurocrine Biosciences is a leading biopharmaceutical company with a simple purpose: to relieve suffering for people with great needs. We are dedicated to discovering, developing and commercializing life-changing treatments for patients with under-addressed neurological, psychiatric, endocrine and immunological disorders. The company's diverse portfolio includes FDA-approved treatments for tardive dyskinesia, chorea associated with Huntington's disease, classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia, hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome, endometriosis* and uterine fibroids*, as well as a robust pipeline including multiple compounds in mid- to late-phase clinical development across our core therapeutic areas. For more than three decades, we have applied our unique insight into neuroscience and the interconnections between brain and body systems to treat complex conditions. We relentlessly pursue medicines to ease the burden of debilitating diseases and disorders, because you deserve brave science. For more information, visit neurocrine.com , and follow the company on LinkedIn , X , Facebook and YouTube . ( *in collaboration with AbbVie ) NEUROCRINE, the NEUROCRINE BIOSCIENCES Logo, and YOU DESERVE BRAVE SCIENCE, are registered trademarks of Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc. title: What Is a Client Portal? A Complete Guide (April 2026)
summary: Learn what a client portal is, why it matters in April 2026, and how to choose the right solution for secure file sharing, project tracking, and communication.
body_text: Your clients expect to check their project status whenever they want, but right now that means fielding the same questions over email multiple times a week. You've tried shared folders, but they don't approach communication or keep things organized per client. What you need is a client portal , and this guide will show you exactly what that means in practice. We'll cover the features that separate useful portals from basic file-sharing tools, how they compare to tools you're already using, and what to focus on when you're reviewing options for your specific business model. TLDR: A client portal is a secure workspace where clients access files, track projects, and communicate without email chaos Security matters: average data breach costs $4.4 million, making controlled access critical for client files Portals differ from file sharing by offering per-client isolation, branded experiences, and built-in workflows AI-powered builders generate custom portals quickly, eliminating the need for developers or templates Stacker generates working client portals from plain-English prompts and syncs with Airtable, Notion, and Google Sheets What Is a Client Portal? A client portal is a secure online workspace where businesses and their clients can share documents, track progress, and communicate without the usual chaos of email threads and scattered attachments. Think of it as a private, branded hub . Clients log in and see exactly what's relevant to them: project updates, invoices, deliverables, and messages. Nothing more, nothing less. You control what each person can access. The core appeal is structure. Instead of hunting through inboxes or chasing down approvals over text, everything lives in one place that both sides can access anytime. Why Client Portals Matter for Small Businesses in 2026 Client expectations have shifted. People want to check their project status at 10 pm without having to email or wait until morning. Self-service access and real-time transparency are table stakes now, even for small businesses. For solo operators and small teams, that pressure is real. Email threads get messy fast, and generic file-sharing tools offer zero structure around who sees what. Security is another growing concern. According to IBM's Cost of a Data Breach Report 2025, the global average breach cost hit $4.4 million. Sending sensitive client files over email is a liability. A client portal closes that gap. It gives clients a professional, organized experience while keeping your communications and documents in a controlled environment. Core Features Every Client Portal Should Include Not every client portal is built the same . Some are basic file-sharing tools. Others are fully structured workspaces. Here's what separates a useful portal from a basic one. Secure file sharing: clients upload and download documents without relying on email attachments or third-party links that expire Role-based permissions: each user sees only their own data, not another client's invoices or proposals Real-time updates: project status, task progress, and messages reflect changes as they happen Branded customization: the portal looks like your business, not a generic SaaS tool Client messaging: communication stays inside the portal, not scattered across email threads Task or project tracking: both sides can see what's pending, approved, or completed The permissions piece deserves extra attention. Without granular access controls, a "portal" is just a shared folder. True role-based permissions let you define exactly what each client, team member, or contractor can view, edit, or submit. That's what makes a portal feel professional and trustworthy. Common Use Cases Across Industries Client portals solve different problems depending on the business. Here's how they play out across a few common industries. Agencies: clients review deliverables, submit feedback, and approve assets without a single email chain Accounting firms : clients upload tax documents and download finalized returns through a secure, organized workspace Real estate brokers: buyers and sellers track deal status, access contracts, and sign documents in one place Consultants: proposals, reports, and project milestones live in a shared space that both parties can reference at any time Construction and home services: contractors see assigned jobs, update progress, and share photos without back-and-forth calls Coaches and trainers: clients access program materials, track session notes, and submit check-ins on their own schedule The common thread is replacing scattered, one-off communication with a single, organized space tailored to each client's specific context. Client Portals vs File Sharing Tools: Understanding the Difference Google Drive and Dropbox are great at what they do. Storing and sharing files is simple, and most people already have accounts. But sharing a folder with a client is not the same as giving them a portal. File-sharing tools are built for storage. Client portals are built for relationships . The difference shows quickly once you try to manage multiple clients. With Drive or Dropbox, every client gets a folder. You manually manage who has access to what, hope no one accidentally opens the wrong link, and still end up emailing updates separately. A client portal treats each login as a context. The client sees their projects, their files, their invoices, and nothing else. No folder structure to explain. No permission misconfiguration to worry about. Here's a quick comparison: Feature File Sharing Tools Client Portals Per-client data isolation Manual, error-prone Built-in by design Branded experience None Fully customizable Task and status tracking No Yes Client messaging No Yes Audit trails and access logs Limited Typically included Workflow triggers No Yes File-sharing tools make sense for internal teams collaborating on documents. When the relationship is external and the stakes are higher, a portal is the right tool. Clients shouldn't need a tutorial to find their invoice. Security and Compliance Considerations Portals handle sensitive data: contracts, financials, health records, and legal documents. That raises the bar for what "secure enough" actually means. Here are the features worth checking for : End-to-end encryption for files in transit and at rest Role-based access controls so clients never see each other's records Audit trails that log who accessed or changed what, and when Single sign-on (SSO) and two-factor authentication options GDPR and HIPAA compliance support, where applicable The audit trail piece gets underestimated. When a client disputes a deliverable or a document goes missing, a timestamped access log saves everyone. Email offers none of that. HIPAA compliance matters most to healthcare providers, therapists, and anyone who handles protected health information. GDPR applies if any of your clients are based in the EU. Not every portal supports both out of the box, so verifying compliance coverage before committing to a tool is worth doing upfront. "Sending files over email is a liability people underestimate until something goes wrong. A portal with proper access controls and audit logging removes most of that exposure." Moving away from email attachments reduces risk in a measurable way. No forwarded threads, no expired links, no files landing in the wrong inbox. Permissions are set once and enforced automatically every time a client logs in. The ROI of Implementing a Client Portal The numbers make the case quickly. Some accounting firms report losing hundreds of hours per staff member annually to manual admin work: chasing documents, resending files, and fielding status questions. A client portal can meaningfully cut that overhead, with firms reporting reclaimed billable time that adds up quickly across a team. That math compounds. Two staff members recovering 150 hours each is 300 hours redirected toward work that actually generates revenue. Client retention adds another layer. Clients who have a clear, organized portal experience are less likely to churn over frustration alone. Miscommunication and disorganization are two drivers of lost business that rarely show up on an invoice, but absolutely show up in renewal rates. How to Choose the Right Client Portal for Your Business Choosing the right portal depends more on your business model than on feature checklists. A solo coach has different needs than a 10-person agency. Start by asking four questions before reviewing any tool. Who are your clients, and how technical are they? What tools do you already use for data, projects, or communication? Do you need white-labeling, or is a generic interface acceptable? How fast does your client need to change? Key Factors to Weigh If your clients are non-technical, the login experience matters as much as the backend. A portal that your clients find confusing will be abandoned, so focus on clean interfaces and minimal client-side setup steps. Integration with existing tools is the other major filter. If your data lives in Airtable, Notion, or Google Sheets, a portal that syncs with those sources saves considerable migration effort. White-labeling deserves weight if brand perception is part of your value. Custom domains, your own logo, and matching color schemes shape how professional your client experience feels. Finally, think about scale. A portal that works for five clients may buckle under fifty. Check whether pricing and permissions grow with your business before committing. Common Implementation Challenges and How to Overcome Them Most portals fail during rollout. The tech rarely breaks. People do. Here are the most common friction points and how to get ahead of them: Client adoption resistance: Some clients will default back to email. Send a short onboarding note explaining where to log in and why. Keep the first experience simple. Staff habits: your team needs a reason to stop using old workflows. Designate one person to own the portal and reinforce it consistently for the first 30 days. Data migration : moving existing documents and records is tedious. Focus on active clients first, archive the rest later. Integration gaps: pick a portal that integrates with the tools you already use. Forcing a full system switch upfront invites abandonment. A phased rollout beats a hard cutover every time. Start with two or three clients, iron out the friction, then expand. Building Custom Client Portals Without Starting From Scratch Building a custom portal used to mean hiring a developer, waiting weeks, and spending thousands. AI-powered builders have changed that equation. You can now describe what you need in plain English and get a working portal generated quickly. The result fits your existing workflow instead of forcing you to adapt to a generic structure or rebuild your processes around a new tool. Instead of choosing between an off-the-shelf tool that's 70% right and a custom build that's out of budget, AI builders let you get to something genuinely tailored to your business. You describe your clients, your data, and your process. The AI handles the structure, and visual editors handle the rest, letting you adjust layouts, forms, and permissions to match how you already work. How Stacker Simplifies Client Portal Creation for Growing Businesses Stacker was designed for this use case. Describe your portal in plain English, and the AI agent generates a working version from that prompt. You can build without needing templates or a developer. Stacker understands what a client portal needs, so you describe your business instead of explaining portal logic from scratch. The result fits your workflow instead of forcing you to adapt to a generic structure. From there, you connect your existing data. Stacker syncs two-way with Airtable, Notion, and Google Sheets, so your data stays where it is and your clients get a proper interface on top of it. Role-based permissions, branded customization, and real-time updates are all built in. One team saved 8 hours per person weekly by consolidating scattered tools into a single Stacker app. Final Thoughts on Client Portal Implementation Moving to a client portal solves the problem of scattered communication. You stop chasing files, your clients stop waiting for responses, and the whole relationship gets cleaner. Pick a tool that connects to your existing data and roll it out with two or three clients first. Book a demo with Stacker to see how the AI builds your portal structure. FAQs What is a client portal in business? A client portal is a secure online workspace where businesses and clients share documents, track project progress, and communicate in one organized place instead of scattered email threads. Each client logs in to see only their own data: projects, files, invoices, and messages, with access controlled by role-based permissions. Client portal software for small businesses vs. file-sharing tools like Google Drive? File-sharing tools store and share files, but treat every client as just another folder you manually manage. Client portal software automatically isolates each client's data, includes task tracking and messaging, provides audit trails, and offers a branded experience that looks like your business. Portals prevent clients from accidentally accessing each other's files and eliminate the folder-structure confusion common with Drive or Dropbox. Can I build a client portal without hiring a developer? Yes. AI-powered builders let you describe your portal needs in plain English and generate a working version quickly. You can then customize layouts, permissions, and branding through visual editors. The result fits your existing workflow and data, so you're not rebuilding processes around a new tool or waiting on a developer to make changes. How do I choose the best client portal software for my workflow? Start by identifying who your clients are and what tools you already use for data (Airtable, Notion, Google Sheets). Pick a portal that syncs with those sources so you avoid migration headaches. Check whether it supports white-labeling if brand perception matters to your business, and verify that permissions and pricing scale as your client base grows. What's the ROI of implementing a client portal? Accounting firms typically recover 40 to 60% of the roughly 300 hours per staff member lost annually to chasing documents and fielding status questions, translating to $5,000 to $8,000 in reclaimed billable time per person each year. Beyond time savings, portals improve client retention by reducing frustration from miscommunication and disorganization that quietly drive churn.

title: Approval Workflows for Regulated Software: Drop the Email Chains (July 2026)
summary: Compliance failures cost $4M per incident. In July 2026, regulated software teams are replacing email chains with in-app approval workflows that hold up to audits.
body_text: Your software team probably has an approval process. The question is whether that process would survive an audit, or whether you'd spend the days before one manually stitching together email threads to prove who reviewed what. Teams in pharma, financial services, healthcare, and legal tech face this problem constantly. Their workflows touch external requirements beyond internal preferences, and an auditor asking to reconstruct six months of approval decisions won't accept a forwarded inbox thread as evidence. The gap is structural. Email, Slack, and shared docs weren't built to produce tamper-evident, version-locked records. They produce noise. When an FDA inspector or SOX auditor asks who approved version 3.2 of a disclosure and when, the answer can't come from memory or inbox archaeology. It needs to come from a system that recorded the decision at the moment it happened. An in-app approval compliance workflow built on review and approval infrastructure fixes this at the source, not after the fact. TLDR: Email chains fail FDA 21 CFR Part 11, SOX, and HIPAA requirements because they can't produce a tamper-evident, version-locked audit trail. Compliant in-app approval workflows require role-based access, immutable audit logs, structured review states, and in-context comments. Compliance failures cost organizations an average of $4 million per incident, and "we used email" is not an acceptable audit trail. When selecting approval workflow software, focus on immutable audit depth, role-based access that maps to your org, and stack integration. Velt is review and approval infrastructure that captures every approval action, comment, and state change inside your app with automatic audit logging. What Approval Workflows Mean in Compliance-Governed Software In industries with compliance requirements, an approval is more than a sign-off. It's a legal record. Whether you're shipping a medical device labeling update, publishing a financial disclosure, or releasing a compliance-gated SaaS feature, every change needs a documented chain of custody: who reviewed it, what version they saw, and when they approved it. That's what approval workflows do in this context. They're not task trackers. They're compliance infrastructure. The gap between "someone said yes over email" and "we have a timestamped, auditable record of who approved version 3.2 of this document" is the gap regulators care about. What a Compliant Approval Workflow Actually Requires Most teams don't realize how many discrete requirements sit inside a single approval event until an audit surfaces the gaps. A compliant review workflow for compliance-bound software typically needs: A clear assignment of reviewers by role, so there's no ambiguity about who had authority to approve a given artifact. Version locking at review time, so the record reflects exactly what the approver saw, not a later revision. Timestamped status transitions, capturing when a review moved from pending to approved or rejected. A rejection and re-review path, because a compliant workflow has to account for changes after feedback, beyond happy-path sign-offs. An immutable audit trail that can be exported or surfaced during an inspection without manual reconstruction. None of this is exotic. But holding it together inside email threads and shared docs is where teams consistently fall short. Why Email Chains Fail Compliance Approval Requirements Email creates a paper trail, but not the right kind. In compliance-heavy industries, approval workflows need more than a thread of replies: they need verifiable, timestamped records that auditors can actually parse. Email chains don't deliver that. The core problems are structural: Approvals get buried in reply threads, making it impossible to confirm who signed off on what version of a document without manually reconstructing the chain. Review tools like email create these bottlenecks by design. Version control breaks down when reviewers work off attachments that have already been superseded, producing conflicting feedback on different drafts simultaneously. There's no enforceable sequencing. A junior reviewer can technically "approve" before a required senior sign-off has occurred, and nothing in the email workflow stops it. Audit trails are incomplete by default. Forwarded threads, BCC'd stakeholders, and replies sent from personal devices create gaps that compliance officers can't account for. Software teams in finance, healthcare, and legal tech face a harder version of this problem. Their approval workflows must satisfy external requirements on top of internal preferences. FDA 21 CFR Part 11, SOX, and HIPAA all have specific expectations around electronic signatures, access controls, and records integrity. Email satisfies none of them reliably. The result is that teams spend hours before each audit reconstructing approval histories from inboxes, forwarded threads, and Slack messages. That's not a minor inconvenience. Research shows knowledge workers already spend 28% of their workweek managing email. In compliance-heavy contexts, the overhead compounds because every gap in the record is a potential compliance finding. The Regulatory Environment Shaping Approval Workflow Requirements Industries with strict compliance requirements don't get to improvise their approval processes. FDA 21 CFR Part 11, SOC 2, HIPAA, and FCA regulations each carry specific requirements around who approved what, when they approved it, and whether that approval can be reconstructed later during an audit. Miss one of those requirements and you're looking at findings, fines, or worse. The pressure has grown. Research shows that compliance failures cost organizations an average of $4 million per incident, and regulators have made clear that "we used email" is not an acceptable audit trail. What this creates, practically speaking, is a set of non-negotiable workflow requirements that most teams are trying to meet with tools that were never built for it. Core Components of a Compliant In-App Approval Workflow Four approval workflow components separate a compliant in-app approval workflow from a loosely connected collection of buttons and status fields. Role-Based Access and Permission Scoping Not every reviewer should see every asset. A compliant workflow ties approval permissions directly to organizational roles, so a junior analyst can comment but not approve, while a compliance officer holds final sign-off authority. This prevents unauthorized state changes and creates a defensible access log. Immutable Audit Trails Every approval action gets timestamped and recorded against a specific user identity. Who approved what, and when, becomes queryable, with no manual reconstruction from memory required. Structured Review States Drafts move through defined review states : submitted, under review, approved, rejected, revision requested. Each transition is explicit, logged, and visible to all stakeholders in real time. In-Context Commenting Feedback attached directly to the asset under review keeps discussion traceable. Comments anchored to specific elements mean auditors can see exactly what concern prompted a revision, and why it happened. Audit Trails in Compliance-Governed Approval Workflows: What Actually Gets Logged When auditors review a software release, they go beyond asking "was this approved?" They want to know who reviewed it, when, what version they saw, and whether anything changed after sign-off. Email chains can't answer those questions reliably. In-app approval workflows can, because every action is captured at the source. Here's what a well-structured audit trail in SaaS actually records in compliance-heavy environments: Reviewer identity and role at the time of approval: an authenticated record, not a name in a CC field that could belong to anyone with inbox access. Exact timestamp of each status change, from draft submission to final sign-off, with no gaps that require manual reconstruction. The specific document version each reviewer acted on, so you can prove no one approved a draft that was quietly edited afterward. Any comments or objections raised inline, preserved in context, not buried in a separate email thread. Regulators under FDA 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and SOC 2 Type II all require tamper-evident records. An in-app workflow writes those records continuously, not retroactively. Approval Workflow Requirements Across Compliance-Governed Industries Compliance-governed industries don't treat approvals as a courtesy step. They're a compliance requirement, and the paper trail behind every decision can determine whether an audit goes smoothly or a product gets pulled from the market. The specifics vary by industry, but the pattern holds across the board. How Requirements Differ by Sector In life sciences, FDA electronic records guidance requires that electronic records include attributable, legible, contemporaneous, and audit-ready approval signatures. In financial services, SOX and FINRA rules require that material changes to reporting or disclosures pass through documented review chains before publication. In healthcare, HIPAA-adjacent workflows often require role-gated access controls tied directly to approval state. What these frameworks share is a demand for three things: A clear record of who approved what, tied to a verified identity, not a forwarded email thread A timestamped sequence showing when each review occurred and in what order Evidence that no content was altered after approval was granted Email chains fail all three. Forwarded threads get trimmed. Attachments get renamed. Reply-all chains branch into parallel conversations with no authoritative record of which version was actually signed off. In-app approval workflows built into the content itself solve this by binding approval state to a specific document version, capturing reviewer identity at the moment of action, and writing the sequence to an immutable audit log. Learn more about keeping approval workflows in your product , not a bolted-on separate tool. In-App Approval Workflows vs. Email Chains: A Direct Comparison Teams in compliance-heavy industries assessing manual review vs automated review options tend to look at the same six dimensions before making a call. Previous sections covered specific log fields and component requirements in detail; this view shows how each gap compounds when multiplied across a real review cycle. The wrong choice can leave your team exposed during an audit or force a costly rebuild six months in. Here are the factors that separate tools built for compliance from those that aren't: Audit trail depth matters more than surface-level logging. You need a record of who approved what, when, and in what context: a full audit chain, not a bare timestamp. Look for immutable logs tied to specific document states. Role-based access controls should map to your actual org structure. Generic permission systems break down fast when you have external reviewers, legal sign-off steps, and internal stakeholders all touching the same asset. Integration with your existing stack determines whether compliance data stays consistent. A standalone approval tool that doesn't connect to your document storage or identity provider creates reconciliation problems. Configurability over rigid templates. Compliance requirements vary widely across industries, and a workflow locked to a specific step count or approval structure will need workarounds the moment your process changes. The short version: if an auditor asked you to reconstruct every approval decision made in the last 18 months, could your current tooling do it without pulling data from three different sources? An in-app approval workflow is a structured review and sign-off sequence built directly into the software where the content or record lives, so every reviewer action gets logged automatically against a specific user, document version, and timestamp. Each step produces a tamper-evident record without requiring manual reconstruction from inboxes or chat threads. title: Grab Responds to Joint Statement by 18 Major Labor Unions: Reaffirms Commitment to Working with Delivery-Partners and Unions to Create a Better Working Environment
summary: Grab is fully aligned with the expectations outlined by the 18 major labour unions, which also reflect the fundamental principles of how Grab works with delivery-partners in all of the markets we…
body_text: Others July 21, 2026 Grab Responds to Joint Statement by 18 Major Labor Unions: Reaffirms Commitment to Working with Delivery-Partners and Unions to Create a Better Working Environment Grab is fully aligned with the expectations outlined by the 18 major labour unions, which also reflect the fundamental principles of how Grab works with delivery-partners in all of the markets we operate in. Grab agrees to and looks forward to implement the four concrete commitments that the unions have requested. Yee Wee Tang, Group Managing Director of Operations at Grab, issued the following statement, in response to the “Joint Statement by 18 Major Labor Unions Across Taiwan”. We are deeply grateful for the valuable feedback and support expressed for Grab’s entry into Taiwan by the 18 major labor unions. We are encouraged by their forward-looking and pragmatic stance in recognizing that the Taiwanese food delivery industry requires a competitor that has the scale, global technology and operational expertise to ensure that delivery-partners will continue to have sustainable earnings, especially in view of the recent global market consolidation. Grab’s mission has always been to create economic empowerment for our delivery-partners and merchants, because we believe that Grab succeeds only when our partners succeed. We are committed to prioritize the livelihoods, well-being, and safety of delivery-partners in Taiwan. If our proposed transaction receives regulatory approval, we are fully aligned with the expectations outlined by the 18 major labour unions, which also reflect the fundamental principles of how Grab works with delivery-partners in all of the markets we operate in. Grab agrees to and looks forward to implement the four concrete commitments that the unions have requested: We will welcome and onboard all delivery-partners who meet our platform’s safety and professional standards to join the Grab platform, and get access to stable earnings opportunities. We will comply with Taiwan’s Delivery Service Act and will continuously invest in creating better systems to help delivery-partners earn more productively and sustainably. We will respect and uphold the right of all delivery-partners to choose the platforms they prefer to work with, and use multiple platforms. We will establish structured and regular engagement channels with local labor unions, and ensure that we listen to the feedback of delivery-partners in different regions and collaborate on solutions for delivery-partners. These are in addition to the Three Core Local Commitments that Grab has set out on 9 June to be transparent about the principles that guide how we support our delivery- and merchant-partners, ahead of our proposed acquisition of foodpanda Taiwan, which remains subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. Our three commitments for delivery-partners in Taiwan address concerns that delivery-partners have around their earnings stability and working conditions. We will ensure Stable Earnings during the transition (including free gear and a dedicated voice hotline that will operate for at least three months to assist delivery-partners through the transition), provide Smart Tools like our technology to reduce waiting times and a 24/7 AI Assistant to maximize on-road efficiency, and maintain a Safety-first environment with in-app features that proactively encourage safe and responsible driving habits. Furthermore, we look forward to introducing GrabAcademy, our holistic training program, to offer upskilling opportunities that support our partners’ long-term livelihoods and professional growth, whether they choose to stay with Grab or eventually explore career paths outside our platform. Grab has spent the last 14 years supporting our delivery-partners and their families’ livelihoods across Southeast Asia, with smarter product features and skills development programs. We look forward to listening and learning on the ground, and becoming a fair and valuable partner to the delivery-partner community in Taiwan over the long term.

1Password vs Azure Key Vault: Which Vault for Which Team (Wire)
summary: They answer one question - what is this integration allowed to read - in different ways. How 1Password and Azure Key Vault…
body_text: Azure Key Vault is now a supported identity source in Wire, alongside 1Password. If you're picking between 1Password vs Azure Key Vault, the feature lists won't help you - both hold secrets, both are encrypted, both are revocable. The real difference is in how each one answers a single question: what is this integration allowed to read? They answer it so differently that the setup, the failure modes, and the governance story all fall out of that one choice. 1Password: the token carries its own scope You create a Service Account in 1Password, grant it specific vaults, and paste the token. That's the whole setup. It's one step because a 1Password Service Account token is self-scoping . The token already knows which vaults it can reach, so when Wire verifies it, the list of vaults comes back for free. Nothing to configure, nothing to enumerate, nothing to keep in sync - the grant lives in the token and travels with it. These aren't plain bearer tokens, either. They carry SRP auth material and an unlock key, because 1Password's model is zero-knowledge: items are decrypted client-side . Wire uses 1Password's official SDK to do that, which also handles region routing - .com , .eu , .ca - off the token itself. Your master password is never involved and never seen. Revocation matches the simplicity: delete the Service Account, and every read fails immediately. Azure Key Vault: you define the scope, because Azure won't Azure takes four steps, and the reason is worth understanding - it's not incidental complexity. There is no data-plane API that lists the vaults a principal can reach. Enumerating them means going through Azure's management plane, which needs a second token scope and subscription-level Reader - a far larger grant than "read some secrets." Asking for it to populate a dropdown would be the wrong trade. So Wire doesn't ask. You supply the vault URLs at connect time, and that list is the scope . Wire refuses to read from any vault outside it, even if the credential technically could. # Step What it is 1 App registration Entra ID → client ID + tenant ID 2 Client secret Copy the Value, shown once 3 Role per vault Key Vault Secrets User 4 Vault URLs One per line - this is the scope Step three is the one people skip, and it produces the most confusing failure in the whole flow. Watch for Key Vault Reader - it sounds like the right role and grants metadata only. You'll be able to list every secret name and get a 403 on every value. Why Azure needs two words for "no" In Azure, authentication and authorization are separate systems. Microsoft Entra ID answers who are you and issues a token good for about an hour. Each vault's own RBAC answers what may you read . A completely valid credential returns 403 on a vault it was never granted. That split isn't academic, and Wire treats the two differently: Response Means Revokes the connection? 401 Entra rejected the principal Yes - the credential is dead 403 No role on this vault No - only that vault is off-limits 404 No vault or secret at that address No 429 Throttled No - honours Retry-After Collapse those two into "access denied" and one missed role assignment tears down a connection that works everywhere else. Kept apart, a missing grant tells you which vault and which role - instead of sending you off to regenerate a client secret that was never the problem. What a secret looks like on each side 1Password has structured Login items: a username field, a password field, URLs. Wire reads the fields it needs and that's that. An Azure secret is one opaque string. It has no fields at all. So Wire exposes it three ways at once - if the value parses as a JSON object, each key becomes a field; otherwise the whole string is available as value ; and every tag is exposed under tag: , namespaced so a tag can never shadow a real field. That mapping is what lets one binding model cover whatever layout you already have - a JSON blob, a bare value with the username in a tag, or two separate secrets - without us imposing a convention on your vault. The Azure Key Vault guide walks through all three. One caution on tags: tags are metadata, not secrets. Anyone who can list the vault can read them. A username in a tag is reasonable. A password is not. The comparison, in one table Feature summary based on 1Password and Azure Key Vault documentation as of August 2026, not independently benchmarked figures. 1Password Azure Key Vault Setup Paste one token Four steps, incl. per-vault RBAC Scoping Token self-scopes You name the vaults - that list is the scope Auth model One system Two - Entra identity + vault RBAC Secret shape Structured Login item One opaque string + tags Credential expiry Optional - you set it, or never Client secret capped at 24 months Granularity Per vault Per vault RBAC, per secret version Regions .com / .eu / .ca , automatic Public, US Gov, China clouds Revocation Delete the Service Account Remove the role assignment Rotation Transparent Transparent So which one Choose 1Password if your team already runs on it, you want to be connected in under a minute, and the people who manage credentials are the same people who'll set this up. A Service Account token doesn't expire unless you give it an expiry when you create it, so there's no forced renewal on a clock. For most teams this is the right answer and the shortest path. Choose Azure Key Vault if your secrets are already governed by Azure, your identity story runs through Entra ID, or you need something 1Password structurally can't give you: per-vault RBAC assigned by the people who already assign roles, secret-level versioning, and sovereign cloud support for US Government or China regions. If a compliance framework asks who granted access to what and when, Azure answers in the system your auditors already look at. The four-step setup is the cost of that, and it's mostly a one-time cost. Do set a reminder for the client secret - Entra caps them at 24 months and doesn't surface the expiry through the token exchange, so Wire can't warn you about it yet. Both are equally safe in the way that matters: Wire holds a reference and an encrypted, scoped token, reads the credential in memory at login, and keeps only the session. Rotation is transparent on both - Wire always reads the current version, so when the value changes in your vault, the next login picks it up. You can also connect more than one. Multiple sources per account is supported, which is how teams run separate dev and prod vaults, or migrate from one provider to the other without a cutover. Once you've picked: the full setup, the provider's own quirks, and what to do when something fails are in the dedicated guides - Using 1Password with Wire and Using Azure Key Vault with Wire . Connect a vault. Both providers are live now. Connecting either takes one pass through your dashboard, and you can run both side by side while you decide. → Get started with Wire · Docs Back to blog

title: News CPI Reports 3rd Quarter Results November 2025 — CPI Aerostructures, Inc.
body_text: CPI Aerostructures Reports Third Quarter And Nine Month 2025 Results November 13, 2025 Third Quarter 2025 vs. Third Quarter 2024 Revenue of $19.3 million compared to $19.4 million; Gross profit of $4.3 million compared to $4.2 million; Gross margin of 22.3% compared to 21.7%; Net income of $1.1 million compared to net income of $0.7 million; Earnings per share of $0.09 compared to earnings per share of $0.06; EBITDA(1) of $1.9 million compared to $1.7 million.Revenue of $19.3 million compared to $19.4 million; Nine Months 2025 vs. Nine Months 2024 Revenue of $49.8 million compared to $59.3 million; Gross profit of $6.6 million compared to $12.9 million; Gross margin of 13.3% (20.4% excluding A-10 Program impact) compared to 21.7%; Net (loss) income of $(1.5) million compared to net income of $2.3 million; (Loss) earnings per share of $(0.12) compared to earnings per share of $0.19; Adjusted EBITDA(1) of $(0.6) million ($3.9 million excluding A-10 Program impact) compared to $5.5 million; Debt as of September 30, 2025 of $15.9 million compared to $18.2 million as of September 30, 2024. EDGEWOOD, N.Y . – November 13, 2024 – CPI Aerostructures, Inc. (“CPI Aero” or the “Company”) (NYSE American: CVU) today announced financial results for the three and nine month periods ended September 30, 2025. “Our third quarter 2025 performance was stronger than third quarter 2024 on all fronts, with improved product mix and efficiencies resulting in 60 basis points gross profit margin increase and a 49% net income increase. In addition, our third quarter-adjusted EBITDA of $1.9 million is 17% higher than third quarter 2024. Our nine-month results remain affected by the Boeing A-10 Program termination impacts of the first half the year. “We also continued to improve our balance sheet during the third quarter, bringing our total debt down to an all-time low of $15.9 million and our Debt-to-Adjusted EBITDA Ratio to 2.6 excluding the impact of the A-10 Program termination,” continued Dorith Hakim, President and CEO. Added Ms. Hakim, “We are also pleased to receive an award from Raytheon, an RTX business, to manufacture structural missile wing assemblies for an undisclosed platform. This single source firm fixed price order with deliveries starting in 2026 represents a strategic win for CPI Aero, adding to our backlog of $509 million as of September 30, 2025. This award continues our success of winning new development programs and demonstrates the confidence top tier companies have in CPI Aero.” About CPI Aero CPI Aero is a prime contractor to the U.S. Department of Defense as well as a Tier 1 subcontractor to some of the largest aerospace and defense contractors in the world. CPI Aero provides engineering, program management, supply chain management, assembly operations and MRO services to this global network of customers. CPI Aero is recognized as a leader within the international aerospace market in such areas as aircraft structural assemblies, military advanced tactical pod structures, engine air inlets, and complex welded products. CPI Aero’s international customer base enjoys a unique combination of large-company capabilities, matched with small-company value, responsiveness, and personal customer service. title: Standard or Low-Calorie: Which Meal Option Should You Pick?
summary: Decide whether Locale's Standard or Low-Calorie meal option fits your daily routine with this clear guide on portion sizes, calorie counts, and flexibility.
body_text: Standard vs. Low-Calorie: The Two Options Side by Side When you build your weekly plan , you are not locked into a single calorie bracket for the whole order. The Standard and Low-Calorie settings are a per-meal toggle, available on most of the weekly rotating menu. This allows busy professionals across the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles to easily customize their nutrition to fit changing schedules and physical activity levels. Attribute Standard Calorie Option Low-Calorie Option Caloric Range 650 to 850 calories per meal Under 560 calories per meal Carbohydrate Profile Full portion of clean complex carbohydrates to sustain high energy levels Smaller portion of carbohydrates, swapped for extra organic vegetables Best Suited For Active individuals, large appetites, or high-intensity training days Calorie-conscious goals, lower-carb eating, or limiting blood sugar spikes Whether you select the Standard or Low-Calorie option, our culinary standards remain unwavering. Both choices leverage nutrient-dense, clean ingredients sourced directly from verified California partners, ensuring your meals are free from seed oils, refined sugars, and the 60+ ingredients on Locale's banned list. It is this unwavering commitment to quality that has earned Locale trust and glowing reviews from high-performing professionals and experts alike, including Connie Chan (General Partner at a16z), Max Lugavere (NYT bestselling author of Genius Foods), Rahul (Co-Founder & CEO of Superhuman), and Alex Mather (Co-Founder of The Athletic). Who Should Pick Standard: Fueling Active and Demanding Workdays Maintaining peak cognitive performance during a demanding twelve-hour workday requires clean, reliable fuel. The human brain accounts for only two percent of body weight but consumes twenty percent of the body's energy [1] , making adequate caloric intake critical for sustained focus. If you regularly engage in deep work, lead lengthy strategy sessions, or transition straight from the office to the gym, your body will burn through low-calorie meals too quickly, leading to afternoon brain fog and fatigue. Locale's weekly plan is built to flex instead. You can customize your weekly rotating menu meal by meal, choosing the Standard calorie option on days when you need robust cognitive and physical stamina. These high-protein meals contain 40 to 60 grams of quality protein and slow-burning carbohydrates like bone broth-infused rice, cooked only with olive and avocado oil, never seed oils. Every meal is packaged in microplastic-free reusable glass jars. The Standard calorie option is ideal for: Professionals managing active daily schedules or high-intensity exercise routines Individuals who need sustained mental stamina to handle back-to-back meetings Anyone with a larger appetite looking for satisfying, clean, high-protein portions Who Should Pick Low-Calorie: Portions Optimized for Clean Weight Management If you are looking to manage weight cleanly, maintain a steady caloric deficit, or simply prefer lighter evening meals that won't disrupt your sleep, the Low-Calorie option is the one to pick . You toggle it meal by meal rather than committing to it across your whole order. Every low-calorie meal stays under 560 calories by replacing a portion of the starches with organic vegetables from California partner farms such as Lakeside Organic Gardens in Watsonville . This lower energy-density swap keeps you fully satisfied without the typical post-meal slump, relying on whole produce to provide natural, blood-sugar-stabilizing dietary fiber. The packaging is worth a mention too, since a lighter meal is still a reheated one: Locale delivers in reusable glass jars rather than plastic trays, and picks them up, sanitizes and reuses them each week. Active weight loss: Effortlessly maintain your caloric deficit while hitting your clean eating targets. Lighter dinners: Avoid heavy starches in the evening to improve metabolic rest and overall sleep quality [2] . Sedentary days: Scale down your energy intake on rest days or during long office stretches without sacrificing nutrition. Designing Your Week: How to Mix, Skip, and Cancel on Your Own Terms Busy schedules rarely follow a perfect, linear routine. On an average day, working professionals spend upwards of 30 minutes just preparing and cleaning up food [3] -time that could be spent closing deals, training, or resting. A flexible meal plan allows you to adapt to these shifts effortlessly without abandoning your nutritional standards. You can easily mix and match both options within a single order to optimize your week. For instance, you might choose Standard meals on intensive training days to fuel your performance, and select Low-Calorie options on rest days. When you build your order from our weekly rotating menu, you choose your meal plan size, which ranges from 4 to 20 meals per week . Every meal is delivered directly to your doorstep in the SF Bay Area or Los Angeles on Mondays, safely packed in insulated tote bags that stay cold for up to 4 hours . Skip any week: If you are traveling or out of town, you can skip any delivery directly from your account dashboard before the weekly cutoff. Cancel anytime: There are no long-term contracts, hidden fees, or commitments, allowing you to cancel your subscription whenever your needs change. Zero-waste system: We deliver your high-protein meals in reusable glass jars and pick up the empty jars each week, ensuring a plastic-free experience . Frequently asked questions What is the calorie difference between the Standard and Low-Calorie options? Locale's Standard meals contain between 650 and 850 calories per serving, making them perfect for those with moderate to active daily fuel requirements. The Low-Calorie option is designed for weight management and lighter dining, staying under 560 calories per serving by replacing a portion of carbs with nutrient-dense, organic vegetables from California partner farms. Do Low-Calorie meals contain less protein than the Standard meals? The Low-Calorie setting reduces the carb portion and adds vegetables, so what changes most is calories and carbs. Protein varies meal by meal rather than following one fixed rule, so check the label on the live weekly menu for the exact macros of the meal you're picking — every meal lists calories, protein, carbs and fiber. Can I mix both Standard and Low-Calorie options in the same weekly delivery? Yes. Because the Low-Calorie setting is a per-meal toggle and not a separate plan, you can mix both options in one weekly delivery. Choose a plan size from 4 to 20 meals and apply the low-calorie option to the specific meals where you want a lighter, lower-carb portion. How does Locale keep meals high-protein and nutrient-dense without heavy calories? We use functional, whole-food inclusions rather than processed fillers to pack in nutrition. For example, we integrate bone broth-infused rice, edamame noodles, and Greek yogurt-based sauces to ensure every meal delivers 40 to 60 grams of protein and over 8 grams of fiber, stabilizing blood sugar and keeping you full longer. How does the Locale subscription work, and can I cancel anytime? Locale operates on a flexible weekly plan with sizes ranging from 4 to 20 meals delivered every Monday in insulated tote bags that stay cold for up to 4 hours. There are no long-term commitments: you can skip a week or cancel entirely at any time through your account dashboard. Where does Locale source its ingredients, and are they tested for toxins? We partner with premium California suppliers like Mary's Free Range Chicken, Lakeside Organic Gardens, and Monterey Fish Market. To ensure uncompromising safety, our meals are independently third-party lab-tested by Light Labs for heavy metals, pesticides, phthalates, PFAS, and other toxins, with the results published. We also pack our meals in plastic-free, reusable glass jars. Sources pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov bls.gov

title: 82% of Auto Dealers Raised Prices Due to Trump Tariffs (Most Want Them Rolled Back)
summary: A new survey of 1,000 U.S. auto dealers shows 82% raised vehicle prices because of tariffs, 75% saw profits shrink, and nearly three-quarters want tariffs rolled back. Higher costs, squeezed margins, and strained customer trust reveal the real impact on America’s dealerships.
body_text: Tariffs have long been a political flashpoint, but a new survey reveals the tangible impact they are having on America’s auto dealers — and their customers. In a poll of 1,000 auto dealers across the country, 82% reported raising vehicle prices because of tariffs , and three out of four said tariffs have cut into their profits . Perhaps most strikingly, an overwhelming majority said they want tariffs rolled back. This survey sheds light on the very real costs of tariffs: higher sticker prices, thinner profit margins, and strained relationships with customers. Below, we break down the findings. Tariffs Are Driving Up Vehicle Prices The survey found that 42% of auto dealers increased prices across all inventory , while another 40% raised prices only on certain vehicles . That leaves just 11% who have not raised prices at all. For consumers, this means the effects of tariffs are widespread: whether you’re shopping for a sedan or a pickup truck, chances are you’re paying more than you would have before tariffs were imposed. Dealers Overwhelmingly Support a Rollback If there’s one area where auto dealers agree, it’s that tariffs should be rolled back. A combined 72% of dealers support reducing or removing tariffs , with 34% strongly supporting and 38% somewhat supporting a rollback. Only 4% oppose, while 24% remain neutral. This kind of near-consensus is unusual in an industry that often divides on regulatory and economic policy. But on tariffs, the message is clear: dealers see them as a drag on business. The Hardest Part: Explaining to Customers When asked about the biggest challenge tariffs create, nearly half of dealers (46%) pointed to explaining price hikes to customers . This is a telling data point. While tariffs are set by policymakers in Washington, the burden of justification falls on the person across the desk at the dealership. Dealers must explain why cars that once cost $30,000 now cost thousands more — often to skeptical buyers. Other challenges include: Sourcing parts (21%) Delayed inventory turnover (18%) But the dominant theme is clear: tariffs strain customer trust. Margins Are Getting Squeezed The auto industry already runs on tight margins, and tariffs appear to be squeezing them even further. 38% of dealers said their margins are significantly lower 37% said margins are slightly lower Only 17% reported no change , and just 8% said margins improved Taken together, this means three out of four dealers have seen their profitability fall due to tariffs . For businesses that rely on steady turnover and financing to cover costs, this decline is not trivial — it directly affects hiring, growth, and long-term viability. Why It Matters Tariffs are often debated in terms of geopolitics and manufacturing policy, but this survey underscores their on-the-ground effects : Consumers pay more at the dealership Dealers lose trust as they struggle to justify price hikes Profits shrink , straining businesses already navigating tight margins And perhaps most importantly, the very people tariffs are supposed to protect overwhelmingly oppose them As the policy debate continues, one thing is clear: tariffs are not just a Washington issue. They are reshaping the economics of the car lot, one sale at a time.

title: Zeta named Retail Banking Fintech of the Year 2022 by Aite-Novarica Group
body_text: Zeta named Retail Banking Fintech of the Year 2022 by Aite-Novarica Group San Francisco, CA – April 28, 2022: Zeta, a banking tech unicorn and provider of next-gen credit card processing, has been named Aite-Novarica’s 2022 Retail Banking Fintech of the Year. Zeta was selected from amongst a large pool of nominations by banking industry stakeholders and analysts at the Aite-Novarica Group. “We are thrilled to be chosen as the winner of Aite-Novarica Group’s Retail Banking Fintech of the Year 2022,” said Bhavin Turakhia, co-founder and CEO of Zeta. “Zeta is fundamentally changing what is possible for credit card issuers with our cloud-native, 100% API coverage, and modern processing stack. We are seeing a tremendous reception to our solution from US issuers and looking forward to accelerating our go-to-market even further this year.” The winners were chosen based on the level of innovation, type and number of customer challenges solved, and the long term market impact and influence made so far. “Zeta is not only one of the newest processing platforms to hit the global stage, but its cloud-native design allows it to meet the needs of both small and large financial institutions and fintechs. It makes sense that voters chose them as Aite-Novarica Group’s Retail Banking Fintech of the Year,” said David Shipper, Strategic Advisor, Retail Banking & Payments, Aite-Novarica Group. To congratulate and officially announce the winners, Aite-Novarica Group is hosting a webinar including a panel discussion with the winners. Details of the webinar are as follows: What: 2022 Banking Fintech of the Year Webinar When: Thursday, May 5th at 11:00 AM ET Where: Online: 2022 Banking Fintech of the Year | Aite-Novarica Contact: To speak with Zeta or request a written contribution, please contact: Rishav Kumar at [email protected] or Haleigh Dhaou at 678-781-7208, [email protected] . About Zeta Zeta helps issuers launch next-gen card programs with its cloud-native and fully API-enabled stack that includes processing, issuing, lending, core banking, and many other capabilities. Zeta has 1400+ employees with over 70% in technology roles across locations in the US, UK, Middle East, and Asia. Globally, eight issuers and 30 fintechs have issued 15M+ cards on Zeta’s platform. Zeta has raised $280 million from Softbank Vision Fund 2, Mastercard, and other investors at a $1.5 billion valuation. Visit us at www.zeta.tech or follow us on Twitter, Facebook and LinkedIn.

title: Scout vs PowerSchool: Smart Compliance Edge for CA Schools
summary: Scout is the AI-native student information system for innovative schools — enrollment, compliance, reporting, and student success in one system schools actually love.
body_text: Scout vs PowerSchool: Smart Compliance Edge for CA Schools Introduction: Navigating California's Complex Compliance Landscape California schools operate in one of the nation's most demanding regulatory environments. The administrative burden associated with state compliance, from CALPADS reporting to independent study documentation, is immense. For school administrators, ensuring accuracy is not just a matter of efficiency—it is critical for securing funding and avoiding audit penalties. To manage this complexity, a powerful Student Information System (SIS) is essential. In the market, PowerSchool stands as a well-known and widely adopted platform. At the same time, modern, specialized solutions have emerged to address specific challenges. Among them is Scout, an AI-powered platform designed from the ground up for the California educational ecosystem. This article provides a direct Scout vs PowerSchool comparison , focusing on the features that matter most to California school leaders: compliance automation, operational efficiency, and audit readiness. By examining each platform's approach, administrators can make an informed decision to best meet their school's unique needs. Understanding the Role of a Modern Student Information System A Student Information System is the digital backbone of a school, centralizing the management of student data, including enrollment, attendance, grades, and schedules. A modern SIS, however, does more than just store information. It acts as an operational hub that streamlines communication, facilitates reporting, and supports data-driven decision-making. For a deeper overview, see the [2025 Guide to K-12 Student Information Systems](https://www.scoutforschools.com/resources/2025-guide-k-12-student-information-systems) . For California schools, an SIS is a critical compliance engine. The system's ability to accurately collect, process, and report data directly impacts state funding and audit outcomes. As regulations evolve, the right SIS transforms compliance from a labor-intensive chore into a streamlined, automated process. PowerSchool: A Comprehensive, Traditional Approach PowerSchool is a dominant force in the K-12 market, offering a broad suite of modules that cover nearly every aspect of school management [4] . Its comprehensive nature has made it a common choice for large school districts that require an all-in-one enterprise solution [5] . Core Strengths and Market Position As an established leader, PowerSchool provides a robust and scalable SIS that serves millions of students. Its core strengths lie in its comprehensive feature set for traditional school operations, including scheduling, grade books, and parent portals. Its ecosystem is extensive, though some find its integration capabilities more limited than those of highly specialized platforms [3] . The PowerSchool Method for CA Compliance PowerSchool addresses California compliance primarily through specialized modules and configuration. This traditional approach requires administrators to run reports, manually verify data accuracy, and perform routine checks to ensure successful data transfers for state reporting [2] . While capable, this process often depends on significant manual oversight and can be complex to set up, particularly for non-traditional programs like independent study. The system architecture is built on established processes rather than proactive, automated workflows [1] . Scout: The AI-Powered Specialist for California In contrast to a general-purpose SIS, Scout offers a specialized, intelligent platform built specifically to solve the compliance and administrative challenges faced by California schools. Purpose-Built for California Schools Scout is engineered exclusively for the unique demands of California's education system, supporting all California public schools and districts. Having started with a strong focus on charter, online, and independent study programs, the platform's features are not add-ons but are intrinsically designed to handle the state's specific requirements for attendance, student engagement, and instructional documentation. The Smart Compliance Edge: AI and Automation Scout provides a smart compliance edge through its sophisticated use of AI and automation. This modern architecture fundamentally changes how schools manage administrative tasks. Automated Workflows: The platform automates the collection and validation of data for CALPADS and other state reports. Its AI proactively detects errors and discrepancies, allowing staff to address issues before they impact submissions. Reduced Administrative Burden: By automating manual tasks like tracking student engagement and pulling work samples, Scout dramatically reduces administrative workload. This frees up valuable time for educators and staff to focus on student outcomes rather than paperwork. Audit-Ready Records: Scout automatically maintains pristine, audit-ready records for independent study programs. It creates a clear and compliant digital paper trail, minimizing risk and ensuring schools are always prepared for an audit. Head-to-Head Comparison: Scout vs. PowerSchool When evaluating Scout and PowerSchool for a California school, the key differences emerge in their core design philosophies and capabilities. Automation & AI Scout: Employs an AI-first architecture designed for proactive error detection and hands-free compliance workflows. The system works in the background to ensure data is clean, complete, and ready for reporting. PowerSchool: Relies on a traditional architecture where compliance is managed through modules that often require manual initiation and supervision.
